_notes: game_state added locally, from a 4-player game driven through the cabinet's streamer.
current_player and current_ball are adjacent in CPU RAM at 0x000366E4 and 0x000366E5, player low
and ball high; the player byte completed 1->2->3 once per ball and the ball byte once.
Scores are 4 bytes on 8-byte centres from 0x02110A24 -- the same base and stride LUCI uses, which
is coincidence rather than a family trait: across the SAM games measured the base takes four
different values and the stride two, independently of each other.
player_count at 0x02110900, the one address every SAM game shares.
Applies to mtl_180h only. mtl_170h is a different revision and needs its own measurement -- SAM
addresses move between revisions, and twd_156c and twd_160h differ in both score base and stride
despite being the same title.
Confirmed after the table exited: 4 players scoring 1,198,400 / 1,175,420 / 1,237,780 /
Free Play was not toggled on this game. Its address is derived, and the derivation is worth
stating because it is testable rather than assumed. Machine adjustments are an array of 8-byte
records from 0x02102008 -- a 32-bit little-endian value, then a byte holding 0xFF minus the sum
of the value's four bytes, padded 0xFF above. Every record in every image checked satisfies it.
Aligning this game's array against a game where Free Play was measured puts it at one of only
two positions across all twenty SAM games examined, and the value there reads 1 on a cabinet
that is in free play. The alignment was validated prospectively: on nba_802 and smanve_101 --
the two games where alignment agreement was weakest -- the address was predicted first, then
confirmed by toggling, and both were exact.
Writing this field requires updating its check byte, or the game discards the change on reload.
The check byte is declared with an explicit checksum address. Without one, a checksum8
record means the checksum occupies the tail of start..end, which is not this layout: here
the summed bytes and the check byte are separate fields of one record.
ball_count and max_credits are derived, not measured on this game: on every Stern SAM game
measured they sit three and one records below free_play in the adjustment array, a rule
confirmed by menu changes with distinctive values on both array layouts (st_162h and trn_174h).
At the derived addresses this game's image reads the factory defaults, 3 balls and 30 credits,
with valid check bytes. Writing either field requires updating its check byte.
checksum16 declared for all fifteen champion records: 36-byte records, initials at +0, score
at +0x18, little-endian checksum16 at +32 as 0xFFFF minus the sum of the first 32 bytes --
start..length 34 covers the summed bytes plus the checksum. All fifteen validate against a
captured NVRAM image. Without these, a writer updating a champion leaves the record invalid.
game_over, tilted and credits come from a 1,091-frame recording of live memory spanning an
operator-menu session and a full game with a mid-ball tilt on ball 2. The session also promoted
ball_count and max_credits from derived to measured: menu values 5 and 9 landed at adjustment
indices 32 and 34 as the free_play-relative rule predicted.
0x00036716 is the status bitfield at ball+0x31, in the same variant as the Pro (mtl_180): 1 in
attract, 42 (0x2A) at ball start, 20 (0x14) in play, 22 (0x16) for the nine samples between the
tilt and the end of the tilted ball, during which player 1's score sat frozen at 696,860. No
single bit separates play from attract or the tilt from the rest, so game_over uses mask 0x30
inverted -- correct in all 1,091 frames -- and tilted is an enum over mask 0x06 in which only
the value 6 is true, the alien_poker precedent. Same declarations as mtl_180, each verified on
its own recording.
credits at 0x0211100C, the thirteenth SAM game at that address.
